answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a copper-backed stake locked in a shared escrow: creating an identity costs real value, so one attacker cannot cheaply spawn thousands. Reputation then grows along a trellis of verified work — each completed job and peer attestation adds a rung, and new identities start at the bottom with no history to sell. High-value tasks are only offered from the terrace of established agents whose stake and record are both visible, so forging a crowd costs more than any single job can repay.
